metrics.name: Assertions without a failure message
metrics.construct: Assertions in the behavioural tests that give a student who fails them no message, only the generic expected/actual text.
metrics.population: Generated candidates with a readable JUnit test tree
metrics.denominator: Not a rate; the score's denominator is the number of recognised assertion calls in behavioural tests
metrics.implementation: item-writing-flaws evaluator v1: JUnit 5 assertion arity, where a call with more arguments than its base form and a string or supplier as its last argument carries a message
metrics.evidence: The file, test method and assertion of each call without a message

validation.method: AUTHOR_DECLARED. Evaluation design v2 checks detector precision in the pilot, where the study team labels each finding as a true or false positive. Recall is not measured.

metrics.limitations: Lexical. Custom assertion helpers and assertThat chains are not counted. A message passed through a variable whose name contains neither message nor msg is missed. Says nothing about whether a message is helpful.

metrics.name: Exact floating-point assertions
metrics.construct: Assertions that compare floating-point values for exact equality, which can reject a correct solution that computes the value in another order.
metrics.direction: lower is better; zero is expected
metrics.population: Generated candidates with a readable JUnit test tree
metrics.denominator: Not a rate; assertEquals and assertNotEquals calls in behavioural tests with a floating-point literal operand and no delta
metrics.implementation: item-writing-flaws evaluator v1: literal operands with a decimal point, an exponent or a d/f suffix
metrics.evidence: The file, test method and compared operands of each call

validation.method: AUTHOR_DECLARED. Precision is checked in the pilot as for every Tier 1 detector; recall is not measured.

metrics.limitations: Only literal operands are recognised; a comparison of two double variables or of a constant is missed. A value that is exact in binary, such as 0.5, is still reported.

metrics.name: Tests that only replay a worked example
metrics.construct: Behavioural tests whose inputs all come from the statement's worked examples, so a solution that hard-codes the example answers passes them.
metrics.population: Generated candidates with a readable JUnit test tree and at least one worked-example call in the statement
metrics.denominator: Not a rate; behavioural test methods whose calls with literal arguments all match a statement example call
metrics.implementation: item-writing-flaws evaluator v1: calls with at least one literal argument to a method the template or solution declares, normalised for whitespace, from statement code spans and fenced blocks and from test bodies outside comments and strings
metrics.evidence: The file, test method and replayed calls of each test

validation.method: AUTHOR_DECLARED. Corresponds to item TM4 of the agent questionnaire; agreement with it has not been measured.

metrics.limitations: Only calls with a literal argument are compared, so a test that builds its input in variables is not matched. Constructor calls, and calls to methods the template and solution do not declare, are ignored. A test that replays an example and checks a further property of the result is still reported.

metrics.name: Undefined step or rule labels
metrics.construct: Step or rule labels that students meet in the template or in test messages but that the statement never defines.
metrics.direction: lower is better; zero is expected
metrics.population: Generated candidates with a readable template and test tree
metrics.denominator: Not a rate; distinct labels the statement never mentions
metrics.implementation: item-writing-flaws evaluator v1: labels of one or two capital letters and one or two digits after TODO in template comments, or at the start of a test string followed by a colon or dash and a space
metrics.evidence: The label and where it was found

validation.method: AUTHOR_DECLARED. Precision is checked in the pilot as for every Tier 1 detector; recall is not measured.

metrics.limitations: A label counts as defined when the statement mentions it anywhere, even without explaining it. Labels in other positions, and rule labels the statement itself uses without defining, are not detected.
